paragraphs.text: Tap your foot on every green light. Only green. Did you tap? She did.
Japan's railway lab set a trap like this. A hundred lights, then red. Twelve people just watch. Five press anyway. Twelve others have to point at the light, and say it. Not one presses.
paragraphs._why: VOICE r4 (Ricks text, lead 16:11): [amused] 0.35 / [amused] 0.5 / untagged 0.5; text = the script's own punctuation (no model_text)

paragraphs.text: After a hundred times, your hand stops waiting for your brain. That's how the cereal ends up in the fridge. Pointing and saying it makes your hand wait. So Japan's train drivers point at their signals, and shout.
paragraphs._why: VOICE r4 (Ricks text, lead 16:11): [amused] 0.35 / [amused] 0.5 / untagged 0.5; text = the script's own punctuation (no model_text)

paragraphs.text: But the shouting rule didn't start as science. The story goes, a steam-train driver's eyes had gone bad. So he shouted every signal to his coal man. His boss rode along, loved it, and made it a rule. He never knew about the eyes.
paragraphs._why: VOICE r4 (Ricks text, lead 16:11): [amused] 0.35 / [amused] 0.5 / untagged 0.5; text = the script's own punctuation (no model_text)

paragraphs.text: New York copied the pointing: subway conductors must point at a striped board. So two New Yorkers held up a sign: "Point here if you are dead sexy." And the conductors had to point. Now try again. This time, point, and say it.
